what: exact W=4 board cycles predicted for the PROTOCOL_2 board runs, written before any of them; per layer CYCLES - IN_STALL must equal "predicted" exactly

protocol.test: a layer is predicted if CYCLES - IN_STALL equals its prediction exactly; every miss is listed

noise: sigma 25 (the manifest's), test_noise seed 0, the board driver's host emulation

board.padding: none: every K (36, 288, 324) is a multiple of 4, so no zero taps and, every window being whole beats, no zero windows are added

core: P = 16 lanes, T = 4 banks, tap t of a window in bank t % 4, sparse mode (mode 1)

rule.count: count_w4 = sum over windows of max(ceil(K/4) + 1, ceil(COUT/16) * max(1, max_b nnz_b), COUT) (denoise/predict_w4.py window_cycles, W = 4, sparse)
rule.fill_drain: conv2..conv10, per board run: min(load, last) + 3 + ((COUT-1) % 16 + 1), load = ceil(K/4) + 1, last = ceil(COUT/16) * max(1, max bank nnz) of the run's last window in the layout as sent (denoise/w4_gaps.py); conv1: the measured constant 17 per run

conv1_constant.source: denoise/w4_gaps.json networks["B-32 ReLU + QAT"] conv1 board_w4
conv1_constant.note: measured on the board on 05.png (the Original), not derived; conv1 reads the image, so its windows are the same in every layout (checked); used unchanged for 06-08

rule.exactness_of_layouts: every layout is the same function: Frozen and Multi-start relabel channels (denoised images identical, checked); the Skew permutes a window's taps and the weight columns together, |partial sum| <= K*127*128 < 2^31 in any order, and every accumulator of conv2..conv9 is the Original's (whole layers, integer oracle, checked)

skew.how: the Original export's windows, conv2..conv9 with their taps in bankperm/skew_count.py skew_order(288, 32): slot s*32 + (p + s) % 32 holds channel p of 3x3 position s (bank (s + p) % 4); conv1 and conv10 unchanged; the weight columns permuted the same way (their config.bin digest is given per layer)
skew.order_meaning: order[slot] = the Original tap index sent in that slot (x_skew = x[:, order])

driver_export_checked.how: emulated with scripts/run_denoise.py denoise (its tap_order path) on every image; each layer's record and config.bin digest must equal the Skew's (checks.<image>.skew_export)

measured_before.status: transcribed from markdown; the raw report.json files are not in the repository
measured_before.note: measured before PROTOCOL_2 (2026-10-18, GPT's runs): Original canary and 3 repeats, Frozen and Multi-start 3 repeats each, all on Set12 05.png; per-layer numbers exist for the Original (canary, repeat 1) and the Multi-start (repeat 1), not for the Frozen. 06.png, 07.png, 08.png and the Skew have never run on the board.

assumptions: one board run per layer: every layer here has at most 65536 windows (16,384 on 05-07, 65,536 on 08.png, the 2x2-unshuffled image), so run_denoise.py --tile 65536 (default) runs each layer once; re-run with --tile N if another tile is used

the Skew run sends conv2..conv9 windows with their taps in skew_order(288, 32) and the same columns of the weights (config.bin digests in runs.skew); conv1 and conv10 exactly as the Original. A host path that sends other windows is not what is predicted
conv1's fill and drain is the 05.png Original's measured 17 on every image and layout (conv1 is not a prediction; its last window's load and compute are listed per image)
CYCLES - IN_STALL is compared; this bitstream's IN_STALL does not count starvation at window boundaries (PROTOCOL_2), so a miss is a miss even with IN_STALL = 0
